places.name: The Poler's Breath
sources: module 20 §12.3b hard-to-reach types (underwater grottoes, air pockets, flooded cellars)
uesp:Lore:Argonian (Argonian physiology: the amphibious advantage the crossing is priced around)

why.founding: The Poler's Breath is a maintained air pocket on the flooded shortcut under the narrows.
why.siteAdvantages: The pocket is the midpoint of a dive that cannot be made on one breath.
why.occupantsMotive: The pocket is uninhabited. Two guiding families keep it up between them. The upkeep is charged into the crossing fee.
why.pressures: Silt is filling the pocket from below. The two families have argued for ten years over whose job the clearing is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the pocket would close the shortcut. It would add two hours to every crossing. The portage crews would take the traffic.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
water at least 6 m deep within 100 m
preferences: landforms: any-channel-bank, oxbow, any-shallow-marsh
water relation: fully enclosed by water
neighbours: inside a drowned or flooded place

boundTo.why: The station and the tidal gate are two parts of one flooded narrows, so they share ground (2026-09-23).

places.traversalFallback: The fallback is to pole the surface route around the narrows. That route takes two hours.

vibe.silhouette: The pocket has no silhouette from outside. Divers find it by diving.
vibe.palette: The pocket is black until the lamp is lit. Then blue light shows doubled in still water. The undressed block is grey.
vibe.materials: The structure uses bog-oak posts, cane walls and bone lintels. Sinew and hide lashing binds it. Peat-tar fills the seams. Crocodile skulls stand on the pile heads.
vibe.signatureFeature: A bell-shaped root chamber holds a bubble of air the size of a boat. The guides rig a pump-line to top up the bubble each season.
vibe.condition: sound, re-lashed last season
vibe.mood: The pocket is a rest stop, used thirty seconds at a time.
vibe.approach: The approach is a descent in the dark to a ceiling of air.
vibe.senses: The pump-line knocks on the roof of the bubble. Rot is held down under cold water. A lamp flame stands perfectly still.

places.whySiteWon: The map point of the air-pocket station is on the bank at its entrance. The old point lay in the water at 2547.1, 4899.5, 1.56 m deep. The nearest dry cell to it is 2522.4, 4924.2, 34.9 m away. That is further than a bank usually lies from the water, because no land lay closer. The point is placed there.

playerPurpose.hook: A room full of air lies halfway through a dive too long for one breath. The guides charge for it as part of the crossing fee.

creatures.note: eels working the pump-line

npcs.note: two polers waiting out a tide

loot.provenance: the guides' own season stores, counted

places.name: The Unmaking Yard
sources: Lore:Nisswo (art made then destroyed); Lore:Sithis (Raj-Sithis the Changer)

why.founding: The Nisswo commission works of art at this ground. The Nisswo destroy each work when the sermon ends.
why.siteAdvantages: The yard is a clearing above the flood. The clearing has one landing. Patrons can attend, watch a work destroyed and leave the same night.
why.occupantsMotive: A resident maker and a rotating congregation use the yard. The maker is paid to make well and then watch the work burn. The Nisswo do not commission a maker who flinches again.
why.pressures: Foreign collectors have begun buying works before their destruction. The Nisswo treat buying before destruction as heresy. The collectors pay in coastal coin. The congregation has learned to want coastal coin.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single sale made public would split the congregation. A second, tolerant unmaking-yard would open on the coast.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
preferences: landforms: enclosed-clearing, flood-high, any-firm-ground, islet
water relation: a landing on still black water
neighbours: near a Nisswo circuit

notableNpcSlots.role: A nisswo who unmakes the work

vibe.silhouette: The debris field looks too deliberate to be wreckage.
vibe.palette: The yard is black above and blue below, with no green. Grey hide is stretched on the frames.
vibe.materials: The yard has no raised structure. Worked bone is set into the ground and left. Gut lashing is used and it stinks. Grave-cairns step up the bank, one course for each death.
vibe.signatureFeature: A field of plinths holds the residue of destroyed works. Each plinth is labelled with what the work was. Each label also says how long the work lasted.
vibe.condition: The yard is clean and ordered. The yard is quiet for its size.
vibe.mood: The mood is unhurried. The burnings are scheduled.
vibe.approach: White plinths stand in black water. The newest plinth holds a work not yet destroyed.
vibe.senses: The pole shudders when it finds bone. Drum-signals carry flat across the water. Tar, burnt cane and ash are trodden into the landing.

places.name: Teeth-Pens

why.founding: The keepers bred crocodiles here for hide and meat. The penned ring itself serves as the cheapest wall in the swamp.
why.siteAdvantages: The creek is gated and once made good pens. The gated creek now works as a trap. Traffic in or out crosses the stock.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers are long gone. The crocodiles left in the pens have gone half-wild. They attack whatever wanders close.
why.pressures: The bridge over the pens is rotting at the centre span. The bridge is the last crossing left into what used to be the village.
why.wouldChangeIf: Draining or breaching the pens would scatter the stock. The crocodiles would spread into the surrounding reaches for good.

neighbours: supplies mounts or protection to a district

places.name: The Hunt Ledge
sources: Lore:Wamasu (Haynekhtnamet of Shadowfen received offerings to stop seasonal flooding)

why.founding: Hunters pay at this shrine for what they are about to take.
why.siteAdvantages: The shrine stands at the head of the reach where every hunt starts. It sits where the reach forks. Every hunt must pass it before starting. Passing hunters keep the keeperless shrine observed.
why.occupantsMotive: Hunters; no keeper.
why.pressures: The offerings have got smaller as the hunting has got worse. The hunters read the smaller offerings as poverty. The villages that eat what the hunters bring back read them as impiety.
why.wouldChangeIf: An empty ledge would be read as the end of the hunting. If the ledge were swept clean, the reach would be declared closed for a season. Four villages would then go to the coast for protein. Those villages cannot afford that protein.

preferences: landforms: oxbow, any-shallow-marsh, ravine, spring-head
water relation: facing the creature's water
neighbours: between a village and a lair

vibe.silhouette: Offerings are heaped facing a body of water or a den. The ground behind the offerings is unbuilt.
vibe.palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. Cane bundles are yellowing. Blue glow shows only where the water is disturbed.
vibe.materials: The shrine uses cairns and driven poles. Cane is used only for the shelter. Vine cord is traded in from the interior and hoarded. The poles are plain and unpeeled. Stone cairns and feather totems stand behind the poles.
vibe.signatureFeature: The ledge records takings as well as offerings. The hunting log is kept as a religious duty. It is the zone's best ecological record.
vibe.condition: New work stands next to work three lifetimes old. The ledge is patched so often that the original work is hard to find.
vibe.mood: transactional piety
vibe.approach: A carved ledge stands over the water at the first bend.
vibe.senses: The air is perfectly still. A slow drum is kept up all night for the dead. Sulphur rises off disturbed mud. Nothing green shows in the light.

places.deferredWhy: The record is deferred as thin rite-dressing. The Kaju maturity ground stands beside it. The Kaju maturity ground carries the same hunt material better.

playerPurpose.hook: The shrine stands at the head of the reach where every hunt starts.

places.name: Since-The-Tree
sources: Lore:Hist (a settlement without a Hist is always political)

why.founding: The village's Hist was killed during the Umbriel passage. The village has stayed put ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: The village ground is good. The villagers stay for the stump. The stump is a relic and a grave. No neighbouring village contests the stump.
why.occupantsMotive: The villagers have no hatching, no naming and no soul-return. They keep the village going anyway.
why.pressures: Their young are Hist-less by birth. The province has no category for this generation. Neighbouring tribes trade with them but will not marry them. Each generation is smaller than the last.
why.wouldChangeIf: Adoption by a neighbouring tree would dissolve them into another tribe. They have refused adoption twice. A hero Hist could hatch their young without taking their name. The elders have not yet put that question to a Hist.

preferences: landforms: flood-high, any-firm-ground, oxbow
water relation: as a hist-village
neighbours: neighbours argue over whether to take them

notableNpcSlots.role: An egg-tender with nothing to tend

vibe.palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. Pale bone is worked and stacked by size. The dead trunk shows no light.
vibe.materials: Bog-oak is salvaged black from the peat and worked wet. Cane-split cord is replaced constantly. Nothing is sealed, since the work is meant to leak. A line of plain poles stands behind the huts where the old field was. The villagers keep the poles upright.
vibe.signatureFeature: The dead trunk was cut down. Its stump is now the village council table.
vibe.condition: New work stands next to work three lifetimes old.
vibe.mood: blunt with visitors
vibe.approach: The villagers seat visitors at the stump table first.
vibe.senses: Mud closes over the foot at every step. Smoked hide and wet bone scent the air. The dead trunk creaks in a wind that the reeds do not feel.

places.name: The Under-Pool
sources: Lore:Wamasu (luminescent organs); Lore:Guar (Glowgill); module 55 (night is authored world state, so night-only places are legitimate)

why.founding: A pool lies in a root chamber. The pool lights blue when disturbed.
why.siteAdvantages: The chamber is closed. Flood cannot wash out the bloom in a closed chamber.
why.occupantsMotive: The pool has no residents. The villages take children to see it once. The showing is a naming custom and not a spectacle. A child who has seen the blue is held to have been seen by the swamp in return.
why.pressures: Taking water from the pool kills the bloom for a season. People keep taking water from it. The takers are alchemists' agents from the coast. The villages will not police the takers. The coin is real and the bloom's death is slow.
why.wouldChangeIf: Repeated harvesting would end the pool. Its end would end the naming custom. The next pool lies more than four days' poling away.

preferences: landforms: oxbow, any-shallow-marsh, cove, sinkhole, spring-head, islet
water relation: still or tidal water, undisturbed
neighbours: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

vibe.silhouette: At night the pool's light is visible from further than any daytime cue in this province.
vibe.palette: The water is black with thin blue light under the surface. Visitors notice the blue is thin. The black mud holds a print for a week.
vibe.materials: The chamber holds raw bog-oak and shell grit. Nothing is lashed. The pool has no marker. The polers say the lack of a marker is deliberate.
vibe.signatureFeature: The bloom lights only where touched. The pool records a visitor's movement for about ten seconds behind them.
vibe.condition: The chamber is worn but sound. Everything load-bearing is new. The wear is all in the same places.
vibe.mood: The pool is the zone's one moment of straightforward wonder.
vibe.approach: The chamber is in total darkness until a hand enters the water.
vibe.senses: Warmth is held in the hide walls after dark. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The air smells of peat, cold and mineral. Silence lies where birds should be.

places.deferredWhy: The record is deferred as the second bioluminescent-water record in a 2.5 km² zone. The blue-flood gallery already carries what the Under-Pool offers.

playerPurpose.hook: The pool lies in a closed chamber. Flood cannot wash out the bloom there.

places.name: One-Spine
sources: Lore:Murkmire (platforms ascending from ground to hover above water)

why.founding: The village is strung along a single walkway. The mire has no ground on which the village could spread.
why.siteAdvantages: The walkway is one firm alignment across two kilometres of mire.
why.occupantsMotive: Households stand in a line, in an order that is also a social order. Position on the spine is inherited. A household's address is its rank. A household moves up the walkway only when a nearer neighbour dies without heirs.
why.pressures: The far end floods first. The poorest households live at the far end. The village repairs from the landing outward. The far end is repaired last in years when the repairs run out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Extending the spine would cost more than the village earns in a decade. The far end has begun talking to the raft people about leaving entirely.

preferences: landforms: any-shallow-marsh, water-narrows, isthmus
water relation: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
neighbours: often the only dry route through its stretch

vibe.materials: Hide and bone cover a trained-root core. The root is failing. Gut lashing holds and stinks. Peat-tar fills the seams. Totems of bone and plumage stand at every landing.

vibe.mood: The village is linear and stratified. Gossip travels end to end in minutes.

places.name: Nine-Stakes Field
sources: Lore:Argonian (pulling a grave-stake raises a bog blight); fauna-hazards dossier (pahnjees)

why.founding: Nine-Stakes Field is a burial field of driven poles. The poles rose after a flood disturbed the burial ground. Nothing was stolen here.
why.siteAdvantages: The field lies on low ground beside a channel. The channel changed course.
why.occupantsMotive: The blights here were raised by no fault of any stake-setter. No wrongdoer can be named. Local law makes the blights the village's debt.
why.pressures: The village that owns the field cannot afford to restake it. The stake-setters price their work by the night. The village pays in rice. The two rates have drifted far apart. The restaking stopped mid-field.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking would settle the blights. The obstacle is labour, not danger. An outsider who supplies the labour buys a permanent claim on the village.

preferences: landforms: any-shallow-marsh, flood-high, any-firm-ground, oxbow
water relation: soft ground, flood-disturbed
neighbours: at or beside a burial field of driven poles

vibe.silhouette: Nine cairns stand in a line. A gap marks where a tenth cairn should be.
vibe.palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. Blue bioluminescence glows in the shallows. Olive weed is matted across the shallows.
vibe.materials: The field has no structure. The bottom is cold silt and the rim is fallen block. Peeled poles are pushed into the bank at a lean. The leaning poles form a warning line.
vibe.signatureFeature: The poles still stand upright and plain. The water carried the dead out from under them.
vibe.condition: The stakes are sound. The ground under them is gone.
vibe.mood: The stake work was done correctly. The channel undid it.
vibe.approach: The stake field is intact. The ground around it has washed out.
vibe.senses: Stake tops knock together when the water moves. Bone clacks on bone in the wind. The air smells of smoked hide and wet bone.

questHooks.opportunity: The stake field drains into water that the seat village drinks. Whatever is wrong at the field shows up in the village's water.

places.name: The Old Cordon
sources: Lore:Argonian (pulling a grave-stake raises a bog blight); fauna-hazards dossier (pahnjees)

why.founding: The Old Cordon is the burial line of a plague cordon. The buriers were foreign. The line was left unstaked.
why.siteAdvantages: The line is an Imperial-era cordon. It runs across the neck of the zone.
why.occupantsMotive: A century of unstaked burial has produced whatever now lies here. The Legion dug the line and left. The ground has had no owner since.
why.pressures: The route that the cordon guarded is still in use. Each generation blames its accidents on the cowardice of the previous generation.
why.wouldChangeIf: Staking the line would take a season. Staking would end a century of accidents. Staking would also settle publicly that the plague dead here were Argonian, not Kothringi.

preferences: landforms: any-shallow-marsh, flood-high, any-firm-ground, oxbow
water relation: soft ground, flood-disturbed
neighbours: at or beside a grave-stake field

vibe.silhouette: A stockade of pikes stands half-swallowed by the ground. It marks a cordon that the stake-readers stopped walking.
vibe.palette: The water is still and black with a slow blue drift. The stake tops are bone-white. The rest is hide-brown and bone.
vibe.materials: The ground is unbuilt. Black water, bog-oak and bone lie sorted by the drawdown. A stripped drum frame stands at the landing.
vibe.signatureFeature: Imperial burial trenches run deep and dead straight. They are cut to a pattern that the villages here do not know.
vibe.condition: The cordon is not kept at all. The trench line is still legible after a century.
vibe.mood: The Imperial work was left where it stopped.
vibe.approach: A dead-straight depression runs across the swamp for two kilometres.
vibe.senses: The air does not move at all. Reeds hiss with drums beneath. A rusted pike smells of wet iron.

places.name: The Carriers' Camp
sources: Lore:Argonian (bones brought to the dirt); Blackrose Chainbreakers (quest plan)

why.founding: The Carriers' Camp is a seasonal camp of bone-carriers. The carriers gather the zone's distant dead. They then walk the dead inland.
why.siteAdvantages: The poling routes converge here. The walking route inland begins here. It is the last point where a laden carrier can be resupplied by boat.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers live here in season. Most carriers are repaying a family's unreturned dead. They earn no wages. The season is worked to exhaustion.
why.pressures: The Umbriel-era backlog of dead reaches this camp too. The stacks show it. Some bundles are labelled for villages that no longer exist.
why.wouldChangeIf: A carriers' strike would leave a season's dead unreturned.

preferences: landforms: any-firm-ground, ford, flood-high
water relation: on a walked route
neighbours: downstream of the carceral sites whose dead it carries inland

vibe.silhouette: Wrapped bundles lie on a rack. A small fire burns beside the rack.
vibe.palette: The water is black over a bone-pale bottom. White shell grit lies at the landing. Blue shows at the waterline. The scene is dark above the waterline.
vibe.materials: The shelters are hide over paddles set as poles. A shelter can be struck in an hour. The lashings are sinew and hide. Tar and ash are worked into every lap. Carved frills are set as boundary markers.
vibe.signatureFeature: Bundles are stacked by how many seasons they have waited. The oldest stack has been rewrapped so often that it is mostly wrapping.
vibe.condition: The camp is sound in season. One set of posts is not sound.
vibe.mood: The carriers do ordinary work among the dead.
vibe.approach: Visitors reach the stacks first. The smell of fresh wrapping cloth follows.
vibe.senses: Wet cloth slaps the rack. The air smells of tar and burnt cane. Nothing green shows in the light.

questHooks.opportunity: The rack is a register of who died where. One bundle came in last season labelled for a village. That village burned ten years ago.

playerPurpose.hook: The carriers wait to carry the dead inland. The oldest bundle in the stack has been rewrapped so often that it is mostly wrapping.

npcs.note: a carrier one bundle short of a full walk

loot.provenance: camp stores, shared with anyone who helps lift

places.sitingNote: The place was cut on 2026-09-04 (round 4 network-role pass). Its identity is a junction: 'where the poling routes converge and the walking route inland begins, the last point a laden carrier can be resupplied by boat'. No such convergence exists in the Naga-Kur deeps. The plotted dot sat 361 m from any route and inside the mercantile-coast culture zone. Rewriting the junction camp as an ordinary camp would have removed the reason it existed, so it was cut rather than moved. Bone-carrying survives in the zone through the necropolis and burial sacred sites.

places.name: The Fallen Meer
sources: Lore:Xanmeer (~15% broken); xanmeer-mesoamerican-reference (ruins subsumed by vegetation)

why.founding: The Fallen Meer is a xanmeer that subsided and broke. It has been looted for two centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: Soft ground took one corner of the xanmeer. The rest followed.
why.occupantsMotive: Squatters and scavengers occupy the ruin in rotation. Worse things occupy it too. Each rotation of squatters believes that the previous ones were too stupid to find the vault. The vault is the ruin's only renewable resource.
why.pressures: Nothing worth taking is left. People keep coming for it anyway. The tended xanmeer downstream now posts a watch. It never needed a watch before.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing changes the ruin, because it is spent. A second subsided corner could open a floor that no visitor has yet reached.

preferences: landforms: flood-high, ridge-end, enclosed-clearing, ravine, sinkhole
water relation: often part-flooded at the base
neighbours: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states

vibe.materials: Cane and hide have collapsed. The bog-oak posts still stand true. Gut lashing stinks and holds. Smoked hide is black and stiff. Crocodile skulls top the pile heads.

vibe.approach: A stone hill leans.
vibe.senses: The air does not move at all. The drum that should answer does not answer. Rot is held down under cold water. Dry ground lies more than a day away.

places.name: Dead-Water Village

why.founding: Dead-Water Village is the seat of the Naga-Kur. The tribe was built for surviving the worst thing in the swamp. The village stands around the tree that made the tribe.
why.siteAdvantages: The village stands on a defensible rise in the inner swamps. Black water surrounds it on all sides. It has a single poling approach. That approach is the tribe's toll. Cargo bound for the eastern swamp is counted at the stage.
why.occupantsMotive: The tribe organises its grave rite, watch and blight-craft around the dead not staying down.

places.name: Deepmire, the Refuge

why.founding: Deepmire is the shelter of last resort. It is a ridge eight metres over the flood. It is hard to reach. Even the tribes avoid it. The presence of Sithis is strong there. It holds pre-Duskfall xanmeers. It holds the skeletons of swamp leviathans. People go up only in an emergency. A few caretakers tend it.
why.siteAdvantages: Deepmire is high, dry, defensible ground. The province has almost none. A single approach can be walked. No approach can be poled.
why.occupantsMotive: The caretakers do not live here. They keep the plateau fit for habitation. They turn the stores each season. They re-roof the shelters each season.
why.pressures: In 4E 48 the need did come. Murkmire's survivors fled onto the plateau while Umbriel passed overhead. The caretakers have fed that memory ever since. The Umbriel Witness Society wants the memorial catalogued. The Nisswo want it let go. The caretakers want it left as it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the argument over the memorial is settled over the heads of the caretakers, the plateau stops being a refuge. It then becomes a destination.

places.name: The Held Vault

places.name: The Sunk Barge
sources: openworld research §3.2 (wreck geometry IS the level; tier by depth and lock)

why.founding: The Sunk Barge is an Imperial-era cargo barge. It went down in the narrows with its load aboard.
why.siteAdvantages: The barge sank in the deep of the bend. It has not shifted since. The hull is intact and the holds are still closed.
why.occupantsMotive: Fish live in the wreck. Divers take a little cargo at a time. A wreck emptied all at once attracts attention.
why.pressures: The cargo is bonded goods. A company that no longer exists still owns the goods. Selling any of the cargo on the coast raises questions.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry cycle would expose the deck. That exposure would end the slow looting.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
in navigable water at least 4 m deep, on the outside of a bend
preferences: landforms: any-channel-bank, oxbow
water relation: fully submerged, hull intact
neighbours: on a poling lane or a hazard

vibe.silhouette: A broken mast stands out of the bend.
vibe.palette: The scene is black above and blue below. Green shows nowhere. White shell grit lies where the bank shelves.
vibe.materials: The barge is keeled timber and iron of Imperial work. Silt reaches the gunwale. Drift bone is laid along the high line of the bank.
vibe.signatureFeature: The barge's cargo seals are intact and still legible. Items taken off the barge carry the mark of a company a century dead.
vibe.condition: The barge is submerged to the deck line. Weed grows on the exposed timbers.
vibe.mood: The barge has been sunk a hundred years. It still counts as the property of its owners.
vibe.approach: A dark mass lies under the bend. It is visible from a boat in good light.
vibe.senses: Cold water presses on the diver. A paddle knocks, then all is quiet. The water is dead, flat and sweetish.

questHooks.opportunity: The barge's cargo seals are intact. Cargo lifted off the barge can be traced to whoever ends up holding it.
